 ACPS closes schools through Thanksgiving break
 The division found incomplete background checks for over 500 employes and are closing its schools to fully resolve the issue.
 By Jackson Hephner November 18, 2026 3:25 pm 
 Facebook 
 X 
 More 
 LinkedIn 
 Email 
 SMS 
 Cville Right Now Albemarle High School 
 CHARLOTTESVILLE, VA ( CVILLE RIGHT NOW ) – Albemarle County Public Schools will be closed from Thursday through its Thanksgiving break, after the division determined that more than 500 employees received incomplete background checks. 
 Acting Superintendent Dr. Chandra Hayes announced the closure in an email to families on Wednesday. ACPS schools will be closed for four days that would have been school days.
 The closure comes after the division found a lapse in its onboarding process over the past three years, allowing more than 500 people to be hired without their backgrounds checks being reviewed by Child Protective Services. The employees underwent successful criminal background checks, but was never reviewed against the Department of Social Services registry.
 “Trust is built through honesty, especially when the news is hard,” Hayes wrote in her email. “The safety of your children must always come first, and I believe this is a necessary action.”
 Hayes said because the affected employees work in schools and departments across the division, she made the decision that all schools must remain closed until the issue is resolved.
 “During a review of onboarding procedures, we found that the criminal background checks were administered, but the personnel responsible for submissions to Child Protective Services did not consistently follow established processes,” Hayes said in the email. “Specifically, over the past three years, there were more than 500 people hired by the division who passed their criminal background checks, but their information was never submitted for the Social Services registry review. We investigated the matter and took immediate action.” 
 She added ACPS’s findings were shared with the Virginia Department of Education, who agreed that staff working directly with children must have their social services screenings completed before they can continue.
 The division is now working with the Virginia Department of Social Services to complete the screenings quickly. Staff who work directly with children will be prioritized by the VDSS so that schools can reopen.
 “If the VDSS review shows that any current employee is the subject of a founded complaint of child abuse or neglect, we will act immediately to protect students” Hayes said. “School Board Policy GCDA requires that such an employee be dismissed once their appeal rights under state law have been exhausted, and it provides grounds for the division to recommend that the Virginia Board of Education revoke their teaching license.”
 A government source told Cville Right Now that VDSS can process about 100 background checks per day. State legislators were being briefed on the situation Wednesday afternoon, the source said.
 Hayes also said that none of the employees currently under investigation or facing criminal charges related to abuse, neglect or failure to report were among the employees whose checks were not submitted. That includes former Hollymead Elementary staffer Michael Swiney, who faces felony sexual assault charges, and former Woodbrook Elementary teacher Nicholas Clark, who faces child pornography charges. 
 Hayes said the division hopes that schools can reopen Monday, Nov. 30, and that reopening will be confirmed on Friday, Nov. 27. The missed days won’t need to be made up because they calendar had built in missed days. If the division is impacted by snow days, that could change.
 ACPS’s afterschool programs are canceled while schools are closed. No announcement was made regarding athletic events.
 “Our goal is to maintain the safety of the students and to do it right,” ACPS spokesperson Jason Grant told Cville Right Now.
